title: Output of the equality hashing protocol
statement: Fix natural numbers $n$ and $k$, let $x, y \in \mathrm{BoolInput}(n)$ be $n$-bit Boolean strings, and let $h \in \mathrm{HashSpace}(n,k)$ be a hash function sending $n$-bit strings into $\mathrm{Fin}(2^k)$. Running the equality hashing protocol on private inputs $x$ and $y$ with $h$ as the shared public randomness returns the Boolean value $\mathrm{decide}(h(x) = h(y))$; that is, the protocol outputs $\mathrm{true}$ precisely when the two hashes $h(x)$ and $h(y)$ agree.
hypotheses_covered: x, y are n-bit Boolean inputs
h is a hash function in HashSpace(n,k)
